title: Climate zones of the world
examples: What is the main difference between a tropical and a temperate climate?
Can you show me where the desert climate is located?
Why do the climate zones change as you go up a mountain?

explain.say: Today we learn about climate zones around the world. These zones show different weather patterns. We will look at four main types today.

draw.text: Climate Zones: Tropical, Desert, Temperate, Polar

explain.say: The tropical zone near the equator is very warm all year. This area receives lots of sunshine daily. Think of places like rainforests in South America.
Desert climates are very dry with little rainfall. Temperatures can change greatly between day and night. The Sahara Desert is a big example.
Temperate zones have moderate weather and four distinct seasons. They are found in the middle latitudes of the world. Much of Europe is in this zone.
The polar zone is located near the North and South Poles. These areas are very cold with little plant life. Ice sheets cover much of this region.
The main difference is the angle of the sun's rays. The equator gets direct, strong sunlight all year. This causes the heat difference.

faq.q: Why is the equator so hot all the time?
faq.a: The equator receives the most direct sunlight throughout the year. This consistent, strong energy input keeps the temperatures high.
asks: What causes the heat at the equator?
Does the equator always have the same temperature?

faq.a: No, some deserts are cold, like the Gobi Desert. The main thing is the lack of rainfall, not just the temperature.
asks: Do deserts have to be hot to exist?
What makes a place a desert?

faq.q: Do temperate zones have rain all year?
faq.a: No, temperate zones have distinct wet and dry seasons. The rainfall changes throughout the year.
asks: Is the rain pattern predictable in temperate zones?
What is the difference between wet and dry seasons?

faq.q: Is the polar zone always covered in ice?
faq.a: Yes, the polar zone is dominated by ice and permafrost. Very little vegetation can survive there naturally.
asks: What kind of life lives in the polar zone?
Is the polar zone always frozen?

faq.q: How do these zones affect the types of plants?
faq.a: The climate determines the life that can grow there. Tropical zones support dense rainforests, for example.
asks: Can I tell the climate from the plants?
What kind of vegetation grows in each zone?

facts: Tropical climates are characterized by high temperatures and high rainfall.
Deserts receive very little precipitation, which is the defining feature.
Temperate zones experience four distinct seasons, including spring and autumn.
Polar regions are extremely cold due to their high latitude near the poles.

quiz.say: A region that experiences hot summers and cold winters is most likely in which climate zone?
quiz.why: Temperate zones are defined by having four distinct seasons, including warm and cold periods.

wrong.0: Deserts are defined by dryness, not necessarily by having four distinct seasons.
wrong.1: The polar zone is too cold to have warm summers.
wrong.3: The tropical zone is warm year-round and does not experience cold winters.

quiz.say: A place that receives very little rain, like the Atacama Desert, is in which climate zone?
quiz.why: The key characteristic of a desert is its extremely low amount of rainfall.

wrong.1: Tropical zones are known for high rainfall, not low rainfall.
wrong.2: Temperate zones have predictable seasonal rainfall patterns.
wrong.3: Polar zones are defined by cold temperatures, not just dryness.

quiz.say: If a location is near the equator, what can you expect regarding the sun's energy?
quiz.why: The equator receives the most direct and concentrated sunlight energy all year.

wrong.1: Indirect sunlight is more common at higher latitudes, like the poles.
wrong.2: While weather changes, the primary energy source from the equator is consistently direct.
wrong.3: Weak sunlight is characteristic of the polar regions, not the equator.
